source_refs.note: Working Principle: a main subheading of 9.21 Light dependent resistor, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 223-223.

blocks.text: The principle used in an LDR is the increase in the conductivity of the material on exposing it to light. In darkness, the semiconductor material has a few free electrons (charge carriers) resulting in high resistance. When light photons hit the material, they transfer energy to electrons in the outer orbits, thus, making them free to conduct electricity. This decreases the resistance of LDR. The amount of light hitting the LDR's surface determines the number of free electrons. Conversely, less light results in lowering the free electrons, thus, making higher resistance. This change in resistance can be measured and used in circuits to sense light levels.
